review.alternative: Preferences could be hard-coded priors rather than acquired transmission.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that agents consistently reject transmitted information in favor of initial internal priors.

claims.statement: Cultural transmission serves as a domain-general mechanism that allows agents to acquire information and behavioral dispositions in real-time.

support.explanation: This establishes that agents can acquire complex behavioral frameworks (a proxy for preferences) through interaction rather than pre-programming.
support.passage: Cultural transmission is the domain-general social skill that allows agents to acquire and use information from each other in real-time with high fidelity and recall.

review.alternative: Observed stability is purely reactive rather than a structural preference.
review.would_change_mind: Findings that dominance hierarchies are entirely stochastic and reset without memory of past interactions.

claims.statement: Dominance dynamics demonstrate that historical interaction sequences create stable constraints on future behavior, effectively forming path-dependent preference structures.

support.explanation: Suggests that interaction history (dynamics) creates stable outcomes, supporting the idea that preferences emerge from the accumulation of specific interactive experiences.
support.passage: The dynamics of dominance: open questions, challenges and solutions.

actions.findings:
Cultural transmission serves as a domain-general mechanism that allows agents to acquire information and behavioral dispositions in real-time. [source-41ed1f7cd5c74426]

Dominance dynamics demonstrate that historical interaction sequences create stable constraints on future behavior, effectively forming path-dependent preference structures. [source-827591d77c6948ed]
actions.limitations: Findings are based on simulation and theoretical frameworks; empirical application to full-scale, open-ended autonomous decision-making requires further validation.
actions.next_questions: How do these emergent preference structures persist when agents are exposed to competing social or environmental signals?
actions.reason: Synthesizes literature on path dependence and social transmission to explain how non-programmed preferences can arise.
actions.summary: This notebook explores whether stable preferences can emerge from accumulated experience rather than explicit programming, utilizing mechanisms of cultural transmission and dominance dynamics.
actions.title: Path Dependence and Preference Formation in Autonomous Systems
